text:
Adam Klapka's biggest moment this season wasn't a goal. On Nov. 19, Quinn Hughes left the Wild's game against Calgary after a collision with him; The Athletic's headline: "Wild’s Quinn Hughes leaves game after hit from Adam Klapka: ‘We hope he’s good’". It put an undrafted Czech forward in the middle of a big story.

His hockey is what you'd expect from a physical depth forward. He has 97 hits in 26 games, 4 goals and 10 points on 12:22 a night, and a heavy shot (94th percentile top speed). His scoring sits near the top of our talent range, and his goals match his expected goals almost exactly.

The worry is the defense. Calgary wins only 41% of the expected goals (chance quality) at five on five with Klapka on the ice, more than eight points worse than without him, and the Flames have won four of their last ten. Evolving-Hockey had him around replacement level last season. He earned his way here as a free agent through the Wranglers, and he plays like it. Hitting gets noticed. The Flames need the shifts in between to go better.
headline: Klapka, the hit and the role
